## Workflow Modelling - Sharp McDermot - 1-58053-021-4

## Why We Had to Write This Book

### Fosdick's Publicity–Usability Curve

As design effort shifts toward marketability the real-world friction for the user increases — highly publicised products tend toward low usability, and the most usable tools are often invisible.


```{python}
#| echo: false
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

BG, FG, SURFACE = '#1e1e2e', '#cdd6f4', '#313244'
BLUE, MAUVE = '#89b4fa', '#cba6f7'

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.3), facecolor=BG)
ax.set_facecolor(BG)

u = np.linspace(0, 10, 300)
ax.plot(u, 10 * np.exp(-0.35 * u), color=BLUE, linewidth=1.5, alpha=0.25)

u_pts = np.linspace(0.4, 9.5, 9)
dpdu = -3.5 * np.exp(-0.35 * u_pts)
lengths = np.sqrt(1 + dpdu**2)
scale = 1.1
ax.quiver(u_pts, 10 * np.exp(-0.35 * u_pts),
          scale / lengths, scale * dpdu / lengths,
          color=MAUVE, angles='xy', scale_units='xy', scale=1,
          width=0.005, headwidth=5, headlength=6)

ax.set(xlabel='Usability →', ylabel='↑ Publicity',
       title='Publicity Vector', xlim=(0, 10), ylim=(0, 10))
for item in [ax.title, ax.xaxis.label, ax.yaxis.label]: item.set_color(FG)
ax.tick_params(colors=FG)
for s in ax.spines.values(): s.set_edgecolor(SURFACE)
ax.grid(color=SURFACE, linewidth=0.5, alpha=0.5)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
